title: Silver’s $60 Floor Is Gone: What Happens Next?
speaker: Jeffrey Christian

macro_themes.view: Run-up to and especially aftermath of the midterms will be treacherous, possibly a hostile Nov-Jan supportive of gold.
CPI and PPI show worsening inflation (headline 3.7%, core 2.6%), concerning for the Fed and Treasury.
Higher rates are a headwind for gold but a bigger headwind for a top-heavy stock market, which becomes a tailwind for metals.
Record stock indices rest on a handful of spurious AI, crypto and data-center names and look increasingly volatile.

calls.condition: Wouldn't be surprised by a spike below 4,000 (to ~3,800) followed by strong buying and a sharp break above 4,200.
calls.reason: Range-bound 4,050-4,200; longer it fails to break up, the higher the odds of a dip, but investors waiting below 4,000 plus political and inflation risk should drive prices higher over coming months, like last Nov-Jan.
calls.quote: while we might see further declines in the near term, over the next several months, we do expect precious metals prices to rise.

calls.reason: Silver broke below its $60 floor and is weaker than gold due to industrial demand headwinds and substitution, but could rise sharply along with precious metals over the coming months.
calls.quote: silver is somewhat weaker than gold. That said, we do think that the price could rise sharply.

calls.reason: Testing whether it can hold a base above 1,600; not sure it can, but more interested longer term.
calls.quote: We're not quite sure that it can. Longer term, we're more interested in it, but ... we may see some price weakness before that.

calls.reason: Weak auto demand, BEV substitution and possibly softening semiconductor demand, with a 2001-style recycling glut analogy.
calls.quote: palladium prices have been much weaker... demand for palladium for use in semi-conductors ... may get a lot softer over the ... next few years.

notes: Platinum/palladium use non-standard tickers PL/PA. Gold short-term is a two-sided scenario (dip then rally), recorded as mixed.
